findings.title: Bounded XML inputs amplify into gigabytes of retained ancestor paths
findings.attacker: Verified public-beta account uploading a crafted device archive
findings.dataflow: POST /ui/devices or /inputs/device → AccountStore.register → RunStore.register → inventory → walk → retained MediaReference.xml_path; comparator also retains full paths in xml_facts
findings.impact: Shared API process CPU/memory exhaustion; hosted API/web container has 1280m memory limit.

line_evidence.evidence: XML limits cover source bytes/depth/nodes/text, not expanded names or derived paths.
Each child gets full parent path plus its tag.
Media matches retain each full expanded path.
Every XML fact retains its full ancestor path.
Async input endpoint synchronously registers/parses input.

findings.static_attack_example: A roughly 200,000-character root name, XForm binary bind /<root>/photo and roughly 9,000 short photo elements referencing the same existing media fit per-XML byte/node limits, but retained paths approach 1.8GB. Reasoned from source, not executed.
counterevidence: Account shared admission lock and storage quota
findings.counterevidence_analysis: One admitted upload expands before persistence/output limits; source bounds do not bound ancestor-name length multiplied by descendant count.
findings.remediation: Bound expanded names, individual paths and aggregate derived-path/fact bytes before constructing/retaining them in shared inventory and xml_facts; add regression.

findings.title: Native Collect metadata query materializes unbounded rows before its limit
findings.attacker: Malicious/compromised explicitly paired device, or malicious copied Collect project selected by operator; ordinary hosted ZIP upload does not reach this parser
findings.dataflow: DeviceTransfer.tick → unpack bounded native tar → write temporary project → scripts.package_collect_project.package → read-only SQLite SELECT * FROM instances WHERE jrFormId=? → list materialization → only then len(rows)>100 rejection
findings.impact: Compact SQLite instances view with recursive/expansive query or computed large values can occupy native transfer indefinitely or exhaust shared API memory.

line_evidence.evidence: Tar bounds do not establish SQLite schema semantics.
Stable paired-device export is copied then passed to package.
SELECT has no LIMIT or progress handler and materializes list before row-count bound.

counterevidence: Native tar40MiB,500 entries,32MiB expanded,10MiB per file
Read-only SQLite; parameterized form selector; identical observations
findings.counterevidence_analysis: Read-only SQLite still evaluates views/expressions; file size does not bound generated output or computation.
findings.remediation: Require expected ordinary-table schema, select needed columns, fetch at most101 rows, enforce connection value limits and deadline-aware SQLite progress handler.

related_inactive_path.evidence: Fixed one-off fixture builder likewise materializes SELECT * before checking exactly one row; not remotely reachable.
